Building basics and creative tools

A whole block is a 1 m cube. Hold Shift to work with half-metre pieces. In creative mode, the brushes build lines, walls, floors and copies in one action, and Ctrl+Z undoes your last building action.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 7 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Place a block

  1. Select a block in the hotbar with keys 1 to 0, or pick it from the Build catalog in creative.
  2. Aim at the face where you want the block. A ghost shows the cell it will fill.
  3. Right-click to place one block. The held item must be a block. With a bow, rifle or throwing rock in hand, right-click aims or throws instead.

A whole block is eight half-metre pieces. In survival, each whole block uses 8 pieces of that material from your pack, and the game says so if you are short. Creative placement is free. Placing blocks

Good to know. If any part of the target cell is occupied, the whole block is refused and the outline turns red. You cannot place a block inside yourself. Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten.

Picking, water and placement limits

In creative, middle-click the block you aim at to pick it. If the block is already in a hotbar slot, that slot is selected. Otherwise the block is held without changing your other slots. Aiming at a door picks the closed door. Middle-click does nothing in survival. Pick a block (middle click)

Your aim passes through water to the first solid block. Stand on the shore and aim at a lake or sea bed, then build up from it. You cannot click the water surface itself. Placed blocks replace water and plants in their cell. Building in and under water

A block is refused, with a message in the status line, when:

  • For ordinary block placement, select a block. Furniture, doors and chests have their own placement steps below.
  • Your hands are empty, or a tool, bow, rifle or throwing rock is in hand.
  • A solid block is in the target cell.
  • In survival, your pack does not have 8 pieces of the material for a whole block.
  • The world already holds 200,000 changed blocks. New building is refused, and the save warns before the limit. What cannot be placed or edited

Flowing water (creative)

The Water block in the creative catalog is a flowing source. Right-click with Water selected to place one. It spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Flowing water does not go away on its own. Flowing water (placing and blocking water)

  • Placing a block into water replaces that water cell.
  • Digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the new gap.
  • Survival players cannot pick up or place water. There are no buckets.
  • The other five water types are blocks. They do not flow.
Tip. To stop unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Half-metre pieces

Hold Shift to place or mine one half-metre piece instead of a whole cube. In creative, press N to toggle detail size without holding Shift; press N again for whole blocks. This lets you keep flying level while building small details. Half-metre detail building

Key or actionWhat it does
Shift + Right clickPlace one half-metre piece.
Shift + Left clickCarve one half-metre piece from a block. Logs and cactus still fell the whole tree or stem.
F1Clean view. Hides the outline, ghost and HUD while you play.
Careful. Holding Shift also sneaks on foot, dives in water and descends while flying.

Doors

Doors are built from boards. They come in three styles and two sizes. A small door is one metre wide and two metres tall, with one leaf. A wide door is two metres wide and three metres tall, with two one-metre leaves. Wooden doors

Choose a door to craft

Open E > Craft and select any door recipe in the Timber section. Three buttons appear above the preview: Style, Wood and Size. Click one, or move keyboard focus to it and press Enter, to step to its next choice. The other two choices stay as they are. Door styles, woods and moves

  • Style: Plain, Panelled or Windowed. Panelled doors have framed, recessed panels. Windowed doors have glass panes in the upper part.
  • Wood: Alder, Birch, Pine, Oak, Fruitwood, Acacia, Willow, Mangrove, Jungle, Cherry, Giant, Palm, Mesquite, Fig or Cypress. A door of a named wood needs boards of exactly that wood.
  • Any boards is the original Wooden door. It takes boards of any wood, mixed if you like, and comes in Plain only. The Style button is greyed out until you choose a wood.
  • Size: 1 x 2 m for one leaf, or 2 x 3 m for two leaves.
  • Changing a choice only selects a different recipe. Doors you carry or have hung, and crafts already queued, stay as they are. If a recipe filter would hide your choice, the filter turns off and the status line says "Showing all recipes".

Costs are the same for every wood:

  • Plain or Panelled, 1 x 2 m: one block of boards (8 half-metre pieces).
  • Plain or Panelled, 2 x 3 m: two blocks of boards (16 pieces).
  • Windowed, 1 x 2 m: 6 board pieces and 2 glass pieces.
  • Windowed, 2 x 3 m: 12 board pieces and 4 glass pieces.

Recipe names follow your choices, for example Oak door, Wide panelled oak door or Windowed birch door. The original two are Wooden door and Wide wooden door.

Hang, open and take down

  • Hold the door and right click solid ground to hang it. The spot needs free space and solid ground under it. A player or animal standing where the leaves would go also stops the hang.
  • Right click a hung door to open it, and right click again to close it. A door swings away from the player who opens it, from either side. It has its own opening and closing sound.
  • The leaves turn on their hinges over 0.35 seconds, easing in and settling gently. If the leaves are not drawn on screen yet, for example while the chunk is still being rebuilt, the swing waits up to one second; a wide door across a chunk edge then turns both halves together. Using a door again while it is moving turns it back from where it stands.
  • A door will not open if anything other than air, water or plants is in its swing path. It also will not open while you or an animal stands where the leaves sweep. Clear the space and try again.
  • An open leaf stands a metre out of the doorway. You and walking animals cannot walk through it, and you cannot place a block into the space it stands in. Undo and redo refuse a change to that space too.
  • You cannot close a door while you stand in its opening. Step out first. A door will not shut while an animal stands in its opening.
  • Mine any leaf to take the whole door down; in Survival, hold left click until it comes down. In Survival the door goes back into your pack if there is room; if the pack is full, it is left hanging. Mining a block next to an open leaf leaves the door standing.
  • In Creative, middle click a door to hold one of the same style, wood and size. This works on either leaf, and on an open door.

Move a door (Creative)

  1. Close the door and wait for it to stop swinging. Put tools away and use ordinary block building, not a brush.
  2. Aim at the door and press Shift + left click. A blue outline marks the original door, which stays where it is for now.
  3. Aim at clear, solid ground. The ghost shows where the door will stand. Press R to give it a quarter turn.
  4. Right click to move the door. The status line says "Moved door | Ctrl+Z undoes".
  5. To cancel, left click or press B. The original door is left as it was.

Ctrl+Z puts a moved door back and Ctrl+Shift+Z moves it again. Finish or cancel a move before you undo.

Careful. The new spot must be empty air, with no water or plants, and every leaf needs solid ground under it. You must move or turn the door, and nobody may stand where it will go. If the status line says "Move only a complete closed door after it stops swinging", close the door, wait and try again. Undo and Redo are refused if the door or its space has changed since.
Good to know. On a server, doors can be hung, opened and taken down once the server accepts the action. In Survival, hanging spends one matching door after the server confirms, and taking one down returns the matching door. In Creative on a server, door moves, Undo and Redo work too: each step waits for the server to confirm, and a move waits while another server action is unfinished. A door move from before you respawned cannot be undone. Blueprints skip door leaves, so a door is not copied.

Wooden chests

A wooden chest is one metre cube of storage. It keeps items where you set it down, so you can leave things at a build site. Wooden chests

  • Wooden chest: one block of boards of any wood. Craft it in the Timber section.
  • Hold the chest and right click to set it down. It fills the metre cell under the ghost, with the latch toward you.
  • Right click a chest within 6 m to open its Chest tab. Your pack and the chest sit side by side. The lid makes an opening sound, and a closing sound when the Chest tab shuts or you walk out of reach.
  • Click an item to move one across. Shift+click moves as much of that item as fits.
  • A chest holds up to 250 kg and up to 64 kinds of item. A world holds at most 512 chests.
  • To take a chest up, mine it. In Survival it goes back into your pack with everything inside, but only if the pack has room for all of it. In Creative, empty it first; you get no chest item back.

Refinish a chest

You can give a placed chest new woods for its body, lid and fittings. Its contents stay inside. Chest refinishing

  1. Equip the Furniture hammer, aim at a placed chest within 6 m, and press E or right click.
  2. The Refinish chest panel opens in the Build tab, starting with oak. Use the Body, Lid and Fittings buttons to choose each wood. Any of the fifteen woods works.
  3. Press Apply changes. Cancel, or closing the panel, keeps the original chest as it was.

In Survival, refinishing costs 4 boards of the body wood, 3 of the lid wood and 1 of the fittings wood: one block of boards when all three match. The old chest supplies the box. Creative is free.

Ctrl+Z turns it back into the original chest with the same contents and, in Survival, returns the boards. Ctrl+Shift+Z applies the finish again. Both need the same game mode, with the contents and woods as they were right after the change. In Survival, Undo needs room in your pack for the boards, and Redo needs the boards again.

A refinished chest is storage furniture. Right click opens it, and it holds up to 250 kg and 64 kinds of item. Empty it before taking it up. Taking up one refinished in Survival returns the chest and its boards. The Chest plan in the carpentry workbench (the Wooden chest plan) makes the same kind of chest from one you carry: in Survival it costs one Wooden chest plus the same boards, and Creative is free.

Good to know. On a server, wait for the server to confirm each chest action. You can set chests down, open them, move items and refinish them in Survival or Creative. In Survival, hold left click to take a chest up with its contents, if your pack has room. In Creative, empty it first; taking it up gives no chest item. On a server, a refinish from before you respawned or reconnected cannot be undone. Blasts, tracks, brushes, copy and blueprints leave chest cells alone.

Furniture and carpentry

Chairs, tables, desks, sofas, kitchen units, bathroom fixtures, storage furniture, beds and lamps are built from reusable furniture plans. In Survival, carry a Furniture hammer from E > Craft > Tools & arms; in Creative, pick a plan in the Build catalogue. Survival pays for the chosen materials when you place a piece. Plans, materials, moving, table joins and lanterns on tables are explained in Furniture and carpentry.

Creative brushes

In creative mode, press B to move to the next brush. The order is Block, Line, Wall, Floor, Replace, Copy, Blueprint, Bench, Railing and Roof. You can also pick a brush from the E > Build tab. Creative brushes (B)

  • Block: Right-click to place one block.
  • Line: Right-click once to set the first corner, aim at the far end and right-click again. The line follows the longer direction. Line, Wall and Floor brushes
  • Wall: Same two clicks. The wall stands upright along the longer horizontal direction.
  • Floor: Same two clicks. The floor stays level at the height of the first corner.
  • Replace: Aim at a block of the material to swap and right-click. Aim at the opposite corner and right-click again. Matching blocks in the box become the block in your hand. Replace brush
  • Copy: Right-click two opposite corners to copy every block in that box except air and the Camp crate. Water and plants are copied too. Right-click again to paste at the ghost. R turns the paste 90 degrees. B discards the copy. Copy brush (copy and paste)
  • Blueprint: Save a build, then place it again. See the Blueprints section. Creative blueprints (save and place builds)
  • Bench, Railing, Roof: One right-click stamps a fixed shape at the ghost. Press R first to turn it 90 degrees. Bench, Railing and Roof patterns
Good to know. Every brush except Block shows a ghost first. One action changes at most 512 half-metre pieces (64 whole blocks). Blueprints have their own limits. If a cell holds a solid block, nothing is built. Water and plants do not block a build. Replace is the exception: it swaps only the material you aim at. Hold Shift on the first click for half-metre steps.

Pressing B clears a corner selection or a copied selection. Copies are lost when you change brush or leave the world.

Blueprints

A blueprint is a build you save and place again. In creative mode it is free to place. In survival, placing it uses pieces from your pack. Blueprints do not work on servers yet.

Save a blueprint (creative)

  1. Press B until the brush says Blueprint. You can also pick it in E > Build.
  2. Aim at a ground corner of the build and press Shift + right-click. The status says First corner set.
  3. Aim at the opposite ground corner and press Shift + right-click again. The Structures panel opens with a picture of what was taken. Nothing is saved yet. Until then, each corner you marked shows a post, and the box that would be saved is outlined. To cancel, press Shift + right-click on the same corner again.
  4. Type a name and press Save. A name that is taken needs a second press to replace it. Keep both saves a copy called Name 2. Closing the panel discards the capture.
  5. If you just placed a saved blueprint, its name is filled in and the panel says Enter updates it. Press Enter, then Enter again, to replace that file. Type another name to keep both.
  6. Aim where you want it. The ghost shows the result. Right-click to build it. The whole build is one undo step, so Ctrl+Z removes it.

Build a blueprint in survival

  1. Press B to take the Blueprint tool out. Press B again to put it away. In survival it is the only build tool, so B is the only key you need.
  2. Aim where you want the build. The ghost turns red when you lack pieces.
  3. Check the list on screen. It shows each material as carried / needed.
  4. Right-click to build. The build is paid for in one go, or refused whole.

Each half-metre piece you change costs one piece of the item that block drops when mined. A whole block is 8 pieces. Dirt-type turf costs dirt. Voxels that already hold the right block cost nothing. If you lack any material, nothing is built or spent, and the status names the missing items.

Key or actionWhat it does
RTurn the ghost 90 degrees.
Page Up / Page DownLift the ghost 1 m up or down.
Left / Right arrowsChoose another saved blueprint.
Delete, twiceDelete the selected blueprint and its file.
Good to know. The save leaves out water, cells you carved out of the terrain and the Camp crate. The status line says how many. A blueprint can be up to 128 m along any side and you can keep up to 64. Placement is refused if it would build over blocks you placed yourself or the Camp crate, or on top of you. Step back and try again.

Saved blueprints are plain files with the `.blueprint` extension in a folder named `blueprints`. The game looks for that folder where it starts. Without it, blueprints last only until you leave the session.

Structure workshop

The Structure workshop is a flat creative world for designing a build away from your home. Choose Structure workshop on the main menu. It is always creative, at midday, with no animals. Your current world is saved first.

Build as you would anywhere, then save the build as a blueprint. Choose Leave workshop to return to the world you came from. The flat ground is never part of a blueprint, and you can travel without reaching an edge.

Good to know. The flat workshop has not been checked in play yet. This page follows the game source and its tests.

Workshops made before this change are listed in Worlds with (legacy workshop). Opening one keeps its original terrain, platform, player position and builds. The main menu makes a new flat workshop and does not change the old save.

Move a build from a legacy workshop

  1. Open the legacy workshop from Worlds.
  2. Save the build as a blueprint (see Save a blueprint, creative above).
  3. Choose Leave workshop to return to your world, then choose Structure workshop on the main menu.
  4. Select the saved blueprint and check its ghost in the new workshop.
  5. Keep the legacy workshop until you have checked the copy. It stays available for more edits.
Planned, not in the game. Sharing or importing blueprints is not in this version. Saving a blueprint in survival is not checked in play yet. They are tracked in the feature ledger.

Structure library

Press O to open the library. Each saved structure has its own picture. The picked one is shown large, with its size and piece count.

Key or actionWhat it does
OOpen the library.
Up / Down arrowsPick the previous or next structure.
DeleteDelete the picked structure. Press it twice to confirm.
EscapeClose the library.

Rename writes the new file before the old one is removed, so a failed rename keeps the original. The library holds up to 64 structures. Click the search field above the list and type part of a name to narrow it. Enter ends the search and keeps the matches, and Up and Down pick among them.

Careful. Checked at Voxelgame 9f915bcb. Not yet play-tested for this guide.

Undo and redo

Key or actionWhat it does
Ctrl+ZUndo your newest step.
Ctrl+Shift+ZRedo it.
Undo and Redo buttonsThe same actions, in the E > Build tab (Creative).

In Creative, undo covers brush actions, blueprints, single blocks placed and blocks or trees you mined. Door moves, chest refinishing and furniture steps go into the same history, so Ctrl+Z always takes back your newest step first. The status line says what it undid, for example "Undid building" or "Undid door move". The history holds your last 32 steps at most. On a server, undoing a door move, chest refinishing or furniture step waits for the server to confirm. Undo and redo building

Good to know. Undo is refused with "Undo blocked" if the cells changed since or if it would put a block inside you. At the save's edit limit it says "Save edit budget reached". It also stops, and says why, where a chest, door, furniture or the Home crate is in the way. Survival block edits and explosions are not recorded, but in Survival Ctrl+Z still undoes furniture steps and chest refinishing; see Furniture and carpentry. History is cleared when you leave the world.

The Build tab and palettes

In creative, E > Build has the searchable catalog. Choose + Tools to open the brush controls, Undo and Redo, four preset palettes and Save palette. Survival gains a restricted carpentry Build tab while a Furniture hammer is in your pack. Creative catalog (Build tab) Build tab and material palettes

  • Click an ordinary catalog item to take one. Shift-click to take as many as fit in your pack. Furniture plans select a reusable construction choice instead of adding a carried item.
  • Right-click an item to remove one you carry. Shift-right-click removes all of them.
  • Middle-click an item to star it.
  • Hover an item and press 1 to 0, or drag it onto a slot, to bind it to the hotbar.
  1. In creative, open + Tools, then click Timber, Masonry, Coastal or Garden to fill the ten quick slots with that set. Slot 1 is selected.
  2. Click Save palette to store your current ten slots.
  3. Shift-click Save palette to load them back.
Careful. A preset replaces all ten quick slots. Click Save palette first if you want to keep them.
